page.title: Why do we conduct science experiments in space?
page.creator: Canadian Space Agency

extracts: Missions to the Moon and Mars mean longer trips and more risks for astronauts, including:
Studying the human body in space for six months gives us data that would take years to gather on Earth.
Canadian scientists use space to study our bones, heart, blood vessels and brain.
On average, there are 200 international space experiments on board the ISS at any given time.
deep_space_risks_listed: longer periods of isolation, very far from home
increased delays in communication with Earth
less ability to rely on Earth for food, materials, and emergency medical assistance
